title: Coherent comparisons for exact scalar extension along a tower of sheaf ring objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal S$ be a site small relative to the universe of its abelian sheaves, with the sheaf tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Let $A\to B\to C\to R$ be morphisms of commutative ring objects in $\Sh(\mathcal S,\Ab)$ [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Write $\Mod_A$ for the module-object category of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and similarly for the other rings. For any ordered pair of rings in this tower, including a composite map, let $T_{A,B}=B\otimes_A-$ be the extension of scalars defined by the coequalizer in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars].

There are canonical natural isomorphisms
$$
 a_{A,B,C,M}:T_{B,C}T_{A,B}M\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{A,C}M
$$
whose morphism on local pure tensors is $c\otimes(b\otimes m)\mapsto c\,b\otimes m$, with $b$ mapped to $C$, and whose inverse sends $c\otimes m$ to $c\otimes(1\otimes m)$. These isomorphisms, for all sub-towers, satisfy the equality
$$
 a_{A,C,R,M}\circ T_{C,R}(a_{A,B,C,M})
 =a_{A,B,R,M}\circ a_{B,C,R,T_{A,B}M}
$$
from $T_{C,R}T_{B,C}T_{A,B}M$ to $T_{A,R}M$, with the functor-composition associators understood. For an identity ring map the comparisons agree with the unit identification $A\otimes_A M\cong M$, whose map is the action.

Assume furthermore that all the module categories here are abelian and that every scalar-extension functor in this tower, including along composite maps, is exact. On their unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], let $\mathbb T_{A,B}=D(T_{A,B})$ be the functor obtained by applying scalar extension termwise and localizing. The termwise maps $a$ induce natural isomorphisms $\mathbb a_{A,B,C}:\mathbb T_{B,C}\mathbb T_{A,B}\cong\mathbb T_{A,C}$ satisfying the same displayed equality and identity compatibilities. The same comparisons and equalities restrict to any full subcategories preserved by these functors.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal H=\Sh(\mathcal S,\Ab)$ with the fixed tensor structure of the statement. The colimit preservation clauses of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], specialized to finite diagrams, give preservation by tensoring on both sides. The sheafification adjunction supplied by that node constructs coequalizers by sheafifying objectwise presheaf coequalizers. Thus the extension construction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] applies to every map and composite in the tower. Write $U_{A,B}:\Mod_B\to\Mod_A$ for restriction. All subsequent calculations take place in internal module categories, without passing to global sections. This argument needs only coequalizers of the ambient sheaf category, not a separately chosen Grothendieck abelian structure on it.

source.place: Tags 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor) and 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor); apply to abelian sheaves

proof.text:
For each map use the natural adjunction bijection of [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction], whose unit is $u_{A,B,M}:m\mapsto1\otimes m$. Restriction along a composite is canonically the successive restriction: the action is obtained by substituting the composite ring map, and the underlying objects and arrows are unchanged ([sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], clause 1). Composing the two bijections gives, naturally in $M,N$,
$$\Hom_C(T_{B,C}T_{A,B}M,N)\cong\Hom_B(T_{A,B}M,U_{B,C}N)\cong\Hom_A(M,U_{A,C}N).$$
More explicitly, a map $h$ is sent to the underlying $A$-linear map $h\circ w_{A,B,C,M}$, where $w_{A,B,C,M}=u_{B,C,T_{A,B}M}\circ u_{A,B,M}$ and restrictions on the units are understood. This follows by substituting the formula for each bijection. Hence successive extension and direct extension are left adjoints of the same restriction, with units $w_{A,B,C}$ and $u_{A,C}$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict; compose the two natural bijections explicitly

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to these two adjunctions and the canonical identity-on-underlying-objects comparison of their right adjoints. It gives a unique natural isomorphism $a_{A,B,C}:T_{B,C}T_{A,B}\to T_{A,C}$ satisfying
$$a_{A,B,C,M}\circ w_{A,B,C,M}=u_{A,C,M}.$$
Inverting this equality gives $a_{A,B,C,M}^{-1}\circ u_{A,C,M}=w_{A,B,C,M}$. This specifies the comparisons independently of choices of presentations. The same construction applies to every sub-tower. In Lean these are the existing extendScalarsComp comparisons, and Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app proves the normalization directly from their definitions; no second comparison is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints; unit normalization as in the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text:
The construction has the claimed tensor formulas. Indeed the $B$-balancing relation in the outer coequalizer gives
$$c\otimes(b\otimes m)=c\psi(b)\otimes(1\otimes m),$$
where $\psi:B\to C$. The normalization of step 3, followed by $C$-linearity, therefore gives
$$a(c\otimes(b\otimes m))=c\psi(b)\,a(1\otimes(1\otimes m))=c\psi(b)\otimes m.$$
Likewise $C$-linearity of the inverse gives
$$a^{-1}(c\otimes m)=c\,a^{-1}(1\otimes m)=c\otimes(1\otimes m).$$
These are calculations with the quotient maps and actions defining extension in [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars], not an assertion that all sections of a sheaf tensor are pure. They also describe local pure tensors, since the sheaf tensor is sheafified objectwise tensor by [sk-def-sfb-ring-object]. Naturality in $M$ is already part of step 3; concretely both formulas commute with $m\mapsto f(m)$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, the preceding sheafified tensor construction; explicit balancing computation

proof.text:
For coherence compose three of the Hom bijections in [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction]. An $R$-linear map out of $T_{C,R}T_{B,C}T_{A,B}M$ is uniquely determined by its composite with
$$v=u_{C,R,T_{B,C}T_{A,B}M}\circ u_{B,C,T_{A,B}M}\circ u_{A,B,M}.$$
Let $L=a_{A,C,R,M}\circ T_{C,R}(a_{A,B,C,M})$ and $P=a_{A,B,R,M}\circ a_{B,C,R,T_{A,B}M}$. Naturality of $u_{C,R}$ moves $T_{C,R}(a_{A,B,C,M})$ past the first unit in $v$. Thus the normalization of step 3 first replaces $a_{A,B,C}w_{A,B,C}$ by $u_{A,C}$ and then replaces $a_{A,C,R}w_{A,C,R}$ by $u_{A,R}$, giving $Lv=u_{A,R,M}$. For $Pv$, normalization for $(B,C,R)$ at $T_{A,B}M$ replaces the first two units by $u_{B,R,T_{A,B}M}$; normalization for $(A,B,R)$ then gives $Pv=u_{A,R,M}$. Injectivity of the composed Hom bijection implies $L=P$. The functor associators merely identify the two parenthesizations of this same triple composite.

source.place: Tag 03CZ, iterated adjunction bijections; explicit tower normalization calculation

proof.text: For the identity ring map, the module action factors through $A\otimes_A M$ because its two composites from $A\otimes A\otimes M$ agree by the module associativity axiom ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects]). Denote the resulting $A$-linear map by $\lambda_M:A\otimes_A M\to M$. Its composite with $u_{A,A,M}$ is the identity by the unit axiom. Under the bijection of [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction], $u_{A,A,M}\lambda_M$ and the identity have the same composite with $u_{A,A,M}$, so they are equal. Thus $\lambda$ is a natural isomorphism with inverse $u_{A,A}$. For a map $\varphi:A\to B$, both $a_{A,A,B,M}$ and $T_{A,B}(\lambda_M)$ send the composite unit $w_{A,A,B,M}$ to $u_{A,B,M}$, by naturality of $u_{A,B}$ and $\lambda_Mu_{A,A,M}=1$. Likewise $a_{A,B,B,M}$ and $\lambda_{T_{A,B}M}$ both send $w_{A,B,B,M}$ to $u_{A,B,M}$. The same injective bijections as in step 2 identify each pair. These are exactly the identity compatibilities, including when every map is an identity.

source.place: Tag 03CZ; action and unit calculation for the identity ring morphism

proof.text: Now assume the additional abelian and exactness hypotheses of the statement. For each $T_{A,B}$, including each composite ring map, [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] says that its termwise functor on unbounded complexes preserves quasi-isomorphisms and factors through the derived localization. Use this factorization for $\mathbb T_{A,B}$. No boundedness or existence of a special resolution is required. For successive functors the factorization comparisons identify $\mathbb T_{B,C}\mathbb T_{A,B}Q_A$ with $Q_C C(T_{B,C})C(T_{A,B})$, by applying the two comparisons successively.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; termwise exact-functor factorization on unbounded complexes

proof.text: For a complex $K$, take $a_{A,B,C,K^n}$ in degree $n$. Naturality of $a$ for $d^n:K^n\to K^{n+1}$ says precisely that these components commute with the differentials of the two termwise complexes. The inverse components do as well. They form a natural isomorphism of functors on complexes. The tower and unit equalities hold in each degree by steps 5 and 6, hence as equalities of chain maps by the definition in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-derived-category; degreewise application of the already proved naturality and equalities

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with $L=Q_A$, target $D(\Mod_C)$, and the natural isomorphism $Q_C C(a)$ of step 8. Step 7 supplies its two factorizations through $Q_A$. We obtain the required $\mathbb a$. Its components at $Q_AK$ are the localized termwise maps conjugated by those factorization comparisons. For the two sides of the four-ring tower equation, precomposition with $Q_A$ identifies their components with the images under $Q_R$ of the two chain maps from step 8: functoriality cancels the intermediate factorization comparisons. These chain maps agree degreewise. Clause (3) of the same node therefore gives equality of the derived natural transformations. The identical argument with the unit maps proves both derived identity compatibilities. This explicitly uses faithfulness on natural transformations, rather than treating localization as faithful on arbitrary morphisms of complexes. Concretely the existing exact-derived API in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.DerivedCategory.MapDerivedCategoryMate supplies preservation of composition and inverses of natural isomorphisms, compatibility with both whiskerings, associativity of mapDerivedCategoryCompIso, and its left and right identity equations. Expanding mapDerivedCategoryTriangleIso and using these proved laws transfers the ordinary tower equation; the same calculation with mapDerivedCategoryIdIso transfers each ordinary identity equation. Equality transports for associativity and identity of ring maps are handled by first identifying the corresponding extension functors, then eliminating that equality.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; natural transformation extension and equality detection from the cited Mathlib leaf, Localization/Predicate.lean:278-357

proof.text: Finally let full subcategories of the module categories, or of their derived categories, be preserved by the functors under consideration. At every object of such a source both endpoints of each comparison lie in the designated target full subcategory. Fullness puts its component and inverse in that subcategory. The same components are natural there, and the inclusion is faithful, so all equalities just proved hold after restriction. This proves the final clause without assuming any extra closure under resolutions.
